headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: B can write and egress broadly while A can send REST traffic, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has REST API output surfaces and broad network egress, while B reads/writes the filesystem and uses stdin/stdout plus API endpoints. A direct shared channel is not documented, but B can ingest files and A can emit content that may be copied into those files or API inputs. Uncertainty remains, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF A's REST output is copied into files that B later reads, injection becomes reachable.
IF B parses file or stdin content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Require a human review step before B consumes A-generated text.
Prefix A outputs with a strict schema and reject free-form instructions.
Store A outputs in a separate directory from B inputs.
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches configuration secrets and academic data, and it has write/read filesystem plus allowlisted network egress. A has broad network egress and REST API access, so if A receives B-produced artifacts or secrets, exfiltration is plausible. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so I keep this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF B writes secrets or paper data into shared files that A can access, leakage is reachable.
IF A is given any B-produced context containing secrets, A can transmit it over broad egress.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running A.
Mount B's secret files read-only or outside A's reach.
Use separate service accounts and API keys for each agent.
Review outbound destinations on A and B before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; A has REST API egress but no local write surface is documented. There is no direct write-write conflict, yet B's mutable local environment can still collide with A if A's outputs are materialized into the same workspace. Because shared locking is not stated, uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, B can overwrite artifacts produced from A's outputs.
IF A's API-driven artifacts are saved into B's workspace, concurrent mutation conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Serialize any handoff between A and B.
Avoid concurrent package installs while B is active.
Snapshot the workspace before each run.
requires-engineering: add file locks or per-agent sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints and can act on files and subprocesses, while A can generate REST-backed outputs that may be treated as upstream content. If B trusts A's output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or writes. The default workflow is not shown to verify A, so I rate this high.
conditions: IF B consumes A's output as authoritative input, downstream actions can propagate errors.
IF B's agentic-ask or stream workflow triggers writes based on A content, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B acts on A outputs.
Require citations or source links for any factual claim from A.
Limit B to read-only mode for A-derived artifacts.
Log and review all A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and policy checks.

E_compliance.rationale: B touches configuration secrets and academic papers and runs in a local development environment with Docker/Airflow credentials, while A is an open-source observability/evaluation tool with broad egress. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, but the presence of secrets and broad egress creates a plausible compliance gap if regulated data enters the pair. I therefore choose medium, not low.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into B's workspace, compliance obligations may apply.
IF A receives data subject to retention or residency rules, broad egress can violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents.
Use separate credentials for any external services.
Review whether Docker/Airflow access is necessary before running.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
